correctness.rationale: The three-class one-point partition is disjoint and exhaustive by ideal/filter closure. For x<y, Lx subset Ly and Uy subset Ux are necessary and sufficient; for x incomparable y, the crossed upper/lower intersections must both be empty. Enumerated family-pair contributions give the exact C_n and I_n identities for every n>=2. Leading exponentials give the claimed exact 6(2/3)^n asymptotic. The supplied independent transitive-closure checker reproduces both formulas for n=2..5, and verifies all pair diagrams for n=2,3; finite verification is corroboration, not an infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The complete-height-two pair theorem expressly assumes all cross-comparabilities. Standard-example bases delete an entire perfect matching, so its closed forms cannot be substituted into that theorem; the strong-amalgamation and ideal/filter generalities supply only the counting representation, not its evaluation. A general algorithm for all finite posets is not a published explicit spectrum or sharp probability for this family.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Prior theorem for fully comparable two levels gives asymptotic 2(9/16)^n, whereas the present theorem for the deleted-matching standard example gives 6(2/3)^n; neither is a parameter specialization of the other. The antichain count has no cross-level relations, convex-set statistics do not encode new-point order relations, and generic one-point encoding supplies only the elementary admissibility rule. The current claim is the entire exact C_n/I_n/T_n spectrum and consequent sharp rate, not the previously known unary S_n formula.

value.rationale: Standard examples are canonical unbounded-dimension posets. The complete and exact three-orientation tuple spectrum reveals a sharp rare-event law and a changed exponential decay constant after deleting a single perfect matching of comparabilities from a complete two-level base. This is a nontrivial, motivated structural comparison; it exceeds routine unary enumeration and its exact leading constant is meaningful in the model-theoretic tuple-type setting.
